title: PrincipalSigned — The Signed Worked Example
note: §7.3.1's worked example exists as a fully SIGNED artifact: `examples/principal_signed_envelope.json`, the first PrincipalSigned envelope in the ecosystem whose signatures are real. Every key derives from a fixed PUBLIC test seed — RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 2 is the human principal, TEST 3 the notary — so anyone can re-derive every byte with no secret material, and the ids and timestamps are the worked example's own values. Three things differ from the §7.3 NotaryAttested shape: `policy.attestation_mode` declares "PrincipalSigned", `policy.delegation_mandate` embeds the parent grant with the human's `principal_signature` verifiable offline, and `proof` is the two-element chain. The three timestamps ascend by requirement, not habit (§7.2.1): the notary decided at :00, the human signed the prepared envelope at :01, the notary countersigned what the human signed at :02. The golden cannot drift: the conformance suite rebuilds it from constants through the reference signing path and byte-compares the result, verifies both envelope proofs and both mandate signatures from the published bytes, and proves the negative — strip the countersignature and the remainder verifies under NO key, because the principal's base is the one-element ARRAY form.
